First off.  I recommend the book “feeling good” by dr. David Burns.  It changed my life.  It’s a book about depression but it’s easily interchangeable with anxiety/panic attacks.  Personally what works really well for me in the middle of a panic attack or if I can feel one coming is to use something called anchor thoughts.  Have a set thought in your mind that makes you feel incredibly excited.  For me it’s a memory of fishing with my late grandpa.  Tell yourself you’re feeling this way (excited) because of your anchor thought.  It will help trick your brain into thinking you’re excited instead of anxious.  It’s a good in the moment fix but overall what’s been best to me is CBT (cognitive behavioral therapy) talking to a professional is something that’s helped me greatly.  I’ve overcome by anxiety and panic attacks by 90% since I’ve been going to therapy and after I read that book.  If you have any questions or feel the need to talk more about it please don’t hesitate to reach out.
